title: ConServe: Fine-Grained GPU Harvesting for LLM Online and Offline Co-Serving
technique: co-serve online + offline requests: latency-aware token-level scheduler sized by a profiled cost model, sub-iteration layer-wise preemption, incremental KV checkpointing for near-zero-cost preempt/resume

optimized_metrics.evidence: an online chatbot may set a 99th-percentile (P99) TTFT SLO of 1.5 seconds and a P99 TBT SLO of 100 milliseconds
optimized_metrics.stat_quote: an online chatbot may set a 99th-percentile (P99) TTFT SLO of 1.5 seconds and a P99 TBT SLO of 100 milliseconds

optimized_metrics.evidence: precisely sizes offline batches and tokens to fit within online latency objectives
optimized_metrics.stat_quote: an online chatbot may set a 99th-percentile (P99) TTFT SLO of 1.5 seconds and a P99 TBT SLO of 100 milliseconds

optimized_metrics.evidence: ConServe is a new LLM co-serving system that achieves high throughput and strong online latency guarantees by managing resources at finer granularities.
LLM serving demands low latency and high throughput, but high load variability makes it challenging to achieve high GPU utilization.

headline_claim.text: ConServe delivers an average of 2.2x higher throughput and reduces online serving tail latency by 2.9x on average compared to state-of-the-art systems.

reported_metrics.where: Fig 2 GPU utilization vs P99 TTFT

metric_definitions.definition_quote: an LLM's serving latency is defined by two key metrics: time to first token (TTFT), which is the duration of the prefill phase, and time between tokens (TBT), which is the execution time of each step in the decode phase
metric_definitions.notes: TTFT described as duration of prefill phase (queueing not explicitly mentioned); TBT = per-step execution time

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Note that TBT is measured per token and is stricter than time per output token (TPOT), which averages the TBT across all tokens per request.
For online serving, following prior work [1], we measure each request's P99 TTFT and TBT.
For offline serving, we evaluate throughput by measuring the number of tokens processed per second, including both prefill and decode tokens.
Utilization is defined as the offered load relative to the GPU's maximum achievable load.

slo_spec: Example SLO: P99 TTFT 1.5 s, P99 TBT 100 ms. In evaluation, 'ConServe's target SLOs based on the P99 latencies achieved by Online-Only' scaled by an SLO scale factor s (attainment reported for s sweeps).
load_regime: request-rate sweep with synthetic Gamma arrivals (CV 0.5; 4096 in / 256 out) plus BurstGPT trace replay; offline backlog always present
tradeoff_acknowledged: Simple preemptive co-serving: online P99 TTFT x3.59 and TBT x3.01 worse, offline throughput 4.27x lower (motivation); non-preemptive: online latency up to 3x, offline throughput down up to 4x.
workloads: BurstGPT (online); DuReader, MultiNews, VCSUM (offline); synthetic Gamma arrivals
extractor_notes: Dual-class objective: online latency percentiles are constraints, offline token throughput the objective. 'tail latency' in abstract = P99 TTFT/TBT. Offline throughput counts prefill+decode tokens (unlike output-only definitions). SLOs relative to Online-Only P99 baseline.

tail_audit.metrics: TTFT @ P99 (1.5 s), TBT @ P99 (100 ms)

load_class_quote: a synthetic online workload (Gamma process, CV=0.5, 2 req/s) alongside sufficient offline requests (§3); BurstGPT trace replay; offline backlog always present
